nodes.claim: Asserts nonuniform convergence using the witness $x=\varepsilon^{1/N}$ and the equality $d(f_N(x),f(x))=\varepsilon$.
nodes.text:
\begin{proof}

    The sequence $\left(f_n\right)_n$ does not converge uniformly, since given $0<\varepsilon<1$ and $N \in \mathbb{Z}_{+}$, for $x=\varepsilon^{1 / N}$ we have $d\left(f_N(x), f(x)\right)=\varepsilon$.

nodes.claim: Offers an alternative nonuniform-convergence argument by invoking Theorem 21.6 and asserting that $f$ is discontinuous.
nodes.text:
We can also apply Theorem 21.6: the convergence is not uniform since $f$ is not continuous.

\end{proof}
